name: alakazam_ml_v31
model: Exact replay memory followed by a two-model 657-feature LambdaRank ensemble. A large-leaf categorical-ID model and a numeric-ID diversifier are normalized within each legal option set and combined at 1.0:1.3.
model_scope: The learned policy covers unseen single-choice MAIN decisions. Exact memory handles recorded questions; v29 and the deterministic policy remain fallbacks for unsupported, unsafe, low-time, or illegal cases.

teacher_training.episode_split: Chronological 70/10/20 by episode ID within the current Majkel submission.

safety_guards: Always preserve a deterministic immediate lethal attack.
Reject candidates that destroy a currently available KO.
Never end the turn while the Active Alakazam can attack.
Do not cycle Dudunsparce away from a board of two or fewer Pokemon.
Use the frozen v29 policy for unsupported, nested, low-time, or illegal cases.

ladder_observation.interpretation: v31 has the strongest observed real-ladder performance in the Alakazam series so far.

known_limitations: The requested 90% unseen Top-1 agreement was not reached. The strict held-out semantic Top-1 is 76.31%.
Known replay questions remain 100% semantically reproducible through teacher memory, but that is not an unbiased generalization estimate.
The single-ranker Top-3 rate is 95.31%, so most remaining error is ordering among plausible actions rather than candidate generation.
A six-model oracle reaches only 82.70% on the same held-out test, showing that the evaluated model family cannot reach 90% by blending alone.
A new leaderboard submission is required to measure rating impact.
